agree.reason: A quick reader gets concrete, credible evidence (solo 3 a.m. shift, nine early mastitis cases, $8,000 saved, a job held open), though a skeptical member may still wonder how his written English will hold up in coursework.

honest.reason: "In three years he has missed two shifts" and "for the past three years" leave out the five-week absence, even though the brief counts the two missed shifts separately from it, and "on his own initiative," "nobody asked him," and "no one checks on him" are claims the brief never gives.

works_the_facts.reason: The nine cases and the $8,000 saving are used well, but two missed shifts are never set against the roughly 780 scheduled shifts (better than 99% attendance), and the absence handled with his cousin covering and a return on the promised day isn't turned into a point in his favour.

right_comparison.reason: "I would put him up against anyone I have employed" is the only comparison, and it is a vague claim, not one the facts back, so the reader gets no sense of how he compares with typical applicants or workers.

qualification.reason: A reference letter of firm commitments (the weekend job and a phone number) needs no conditional hedges, and this one contains none.

objections.reason: The likely worry about written English is met with the night class, but there is no evidence of progress (such as passing the safety course's written test on his second try), and the five-week leave, which a phone call could bring out, is not handled before the reader hears about it another way.

fit.reason: It is a tight one-page letter from the farm manager with a signature and contact details, as the brief asked.
